title: Devices
subtitle: Everything on your local network — who it is, what it's running, and how it's behaving.
emptyDesc: Clarity looks up devices over mDNS, the ARP cache, SSDP, NetBIOS and ping. Run a scan to populate the list.
demoModeHint: Mask hostnames, MAC tails, IPv6 and process names so a screenshot is safe to share. IPv4 stays visible — private ranges leak nothing.
alertsEmpty: No alerts yet — Clarity raises one when a device joins, leaves, or opens a port.
detailEmptyDesc: Pick a device from the list to inspect its identity, services, link quality and history.
linkUnavailable: No measurements yet — run a probe or measure now.
linkWakeUp: The first reply took much longer than the ones behind it. That's a device letting its Wi-Fi radio sleep between frames and having to wake up to answer — normal for anything battery-powered.
linkNotSignal: This is the path between your computer and the device, not the device's own Wi-Fi signal. No app can read that: signal is measured by whichever radio is receiving.
portStateEmpty: This device has never been probed. Use Probe Ports to check the catalog, or run a network-wide scan from Security.
portsFilteredExplainer: {{count}} port(s) timed out. Closed is a definite "nothing is listening"; filtered means something dropped the probe, so what's behind it is unknown.

portState.open: Open — the service is actively listening
portState.closed: Closed — the device answered, refusing the connection
portState.filtered: Filtered — no answer at all, the probe timed out

inspectExplainer: Inspection reads only what the service volunteers on connect — a web server's response header, an SSH identification line, a database's handshake. Clarity never logs in, sends a password, or issues a command.
rawEmpty: Nothing read yet — use Inspect service to look inside this port.
fullScanFailed: The scan could not be started.
fullScanNoIp: This device has no IPv4 address to scan.
fullScanRangeInvalid: Enter a range between 1 and 65535, low to high.
fullScanIdle: The catalog walk checks a curated set of well-known ports. A full scan connects to every port in the range to find open services the catalog missed — heavier by design, so it's always started by hand, per device.
localOnlyHint: Bound to a loopback address, so nothing else on your network can connect — not another computer, not your phone, not the router. These are the ones no network probe could ever have shown you.
localReachableHint: Not bound to loopback, so anything on your Wi-Fi can reach them. Usually intended — file sharing and remote access work this way — but worth a glance for one you don't recognise.
